title: No Determination | Unknown Disruption Code | UK Regime (UK Departure) + APPR | Delay 4+ hrs (5h) | Basic Aeroplan
goal:
Flight AC 865 LHR ? YUL flew but arrived 5 hours late (4+ hours band seen in ADS/AODB). The trip starts in the UK, so the UK regime (EU 261 UK branch) applies. APPR also applies because the flight lands in Canada. A disruption code is logged, but DDS doesn't recognize it, so it can't be classed as Controllable or Uncontrollable under either regime. The passenger has a Basic Aeroplan profile (9876543210) on the booking. This is different from the NULL/missing code case, which waits and re-checks for 14 days. Here a code exists but can't be mapped, so DDS returns NO DETERMINATION straight away. The chatbot shows the standard ND-X02 message, and the case is created automatically for manual review with a 30-day response commitment.
Validates: (1) DDS treats an UNKNOWN code differently from a NULL code for a UK departure, (2) No Determination comes back straight away with no 14-day re-check, (3) the chatbot shows the standard ND-X02 message, (4) the case is created and sent to manual review without asking the customer to confirm, (5) no Cash or AC Wallet offer is made even though Basic Aeroplan is linked, (6) the UK 6-year filing limit is used.
